newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends soft on rollovers, liquidation.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends soft on rollovers, liquidation.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed lower on Tuesday amid July/September rollovers and speculative liquidation.

July ended down nine stg at 1,017 stg per tonne and September lost six to 1,038. Total volume stood at 7,259 lots, up from Monday's turnover. July led volume with 3,542 contracts, followed by September's 2,232. All other months tallied fewer than 1,000 lots each.
Traders attributed most activity to rolling over of July positions into September, which helped widen the spread to 21 stg.
A large European firm was seen crossing about 900 lots at 20 and a U.S. firm crossing about 500 to make up the bulk of volume. They speculated the trades were done for funds.

After the day's action, traders were mixed on cocoa's near-time direction. Some expected more losses because speculators in New York still had more long positions to liquidate before first notice day there on June 17.
Technically, others said July's close below 1,019 was also negative and should provide a path for a test of support at 1,000.
But optimists said the markets were braced for first notice day and have already priced in a downturn. Now, they said prices should edge up again.
In options, no July contracts traded.
